title: ACS predicate DSL: no absence primitive, and the eval-quality lint cannot flag unsatisfiable-by-construction predicates (positive primitive asserting an absence)
summary: Cycle-1488 (batch-20260816b) FAILed on its own TDD-authored predicate TestC1488_003: FileContains(phase_bindings.go, 'worktreeTree == headTree') written to assert the string is ABSENT — a positive primitive for an absence claim, red in every possible tree state. The lane burned a full spine proving an unsatisfiable acceptance. SECOND instance of the self-authored-unsatisfiable-contract family (first: cycle-1480/1483 minted KindJSON contract demanding pure-JSON AND a sentinel tail — see minted-phase-verdict-contract-unsatisfiable, parked). SECOND burn: cycle-1492 (the retry) inherited the same unrepaired predicate and red-counted on it despite all-new-work-green — one unsatisfiable predicate has now cost two full lanes.
root_cause: The predicate DSL offers positive primitives (FileContains) with no first-class negation, so absence assertions get mis-encoded; and the eval-quality/flaky-shape pre-flight has no unsatisfiability check — a predicate that cannot green under ANY tree state passes authoring review and is only discovered by burning the cycle.
fix: (1) Add the absence primitive (FileNotContains or a Negate combinator) to the ACS predicate vocabulary — smallest change that lets authors say what they mean. (2) Extend the eval-quality pre-flight with an unsatisfiability lint: for each authored predicate, detect the positive-primitive-with-absence-intent shape (e.g. the failure detail text or expectation naming 'missing'/'absent'/'not contain' while using a Contains-family primitive) and WARN/BLOCK at authoring time, before dispatch. (3) Regression: the exact TestC1488_003 shape red-first through the lint.
